chapter_theme: The praise of the guru closes with his sovereignty and silence: his own law his only law, a Siva-yogi of silence who never opens his mouth in anger, the disciple of Chitrambalavan, the knowledge-light with no name, the Karunai Ananda muni who rains bliss and quenches maya's glare, beyond the reach of ida, pingala and the sushumna. Then the poet speaks in his own voice: called a libertine, with enemies everywhere, he wept his way to the guru's country, found the town Kayapuri and settled there, where the Lady Sivananda Valli, Trikonavalli, raised the daughter of kutilai and set her to the art of the staff-dance, making her puppet dance through every sect and scripture until, like a cloud that has flashed, she cooled and knew herself.
structure_note: 2195 to 2206 end the guru's epithets, from his self-law to Chitrambalam's lotus feet; 2207 to 2211 are the poet's own arrival at Kayapuri and the Lady who names and raises the girl; 2212 to 2219 are the girl's training in dance, sects and scriptures, ending in self-knowledge and the old woman who turns to instruct her (which chapter 113 carries). The units remain two-line slices of one kalivenba, and the identity of the girl is the poem's cipher.

2195.reading: His own command is the only command upon himself; he has no other law over him; and for all time (2196) his fame does not change.
2195.nuance: The guru's autonomy is the claim: no scripture, sect or god rules him, which the attacks of 2181 and 2221 to 2233 presuppose.

2196.reading: He of unchanging fame and the honey garland, the Siva-yogi of silence who does not open his mouth to rage; and straight (2197) his guru is Chitrambalavan.
2196.nuance: வாய்திறந்து சீறாத: silence is defined as not opening the mouth in anger, a narrower and more practical mounam than the stilling of all thought. Yet 2194 gave him fury; the anger is turned on the disciples' enemies, not spoken.

2197.reading: He whose two feet were raised seeking the grace of the feet of the guru who ruled him, Chitrambalavan; and (2198) he wears the garb of Siva.
2197.nuance: சிற்றம்பலவன் is the Lord of the little hall at Chidambaram and also, here, the name or title of the guru's own guru; the poem does not separate the two. இருபதத்தான் is read as the one of two feet; it could also be the one of two states.

2198.reading: Wearing Siva's garb, he rises and shines on the seat of the rich lotus, Jnanaprakasan, the light of knowledge; and if he moves (2199)...
2198.nuance: ஞானப் பிரகாசன் may be a title or the guru's proper name; a Gnanaprakasar is known among Chidambaram teachers, but the poem gives no date. The lotus seat is the yogi's posture and the heart-lotus of 2150. ஆடில் carries into 2199 and its sense there is unclear.

2199.reading: He is the horse and the skin, the hungry and the sodden (?), the great and the rare, the one without a name; and turiya (2200) he passes beyond.
2199.nuance: A chain of rhymed epithets whose sense is mostly sound: பரியான் (horse, or 'large'), உரியான் (skin, or 'fitting'), பசியான், பொசியான். The last three words are the firm ones: great, rare, nameless. பரி recalls the horse of 2188, and turiya at the unit's end connects to 2200's list of what he has passed.

2200.reading: Beyond turiya and its faults, beyond the shining space, beyond knowledge itself, stands the one of the golden feet; and cool (2201) is the muni of compassion.
2200.nuance: தீதம் கடந்து is read as beyond faults; தீதம் may be an error for அதீதம், the state past turiya, which would make the first two words 'beyond turiya-atita'. Either way the guru is placed beyond the highest avastha and beyond போதம், knowledge, as 2168 placed Siva beyond light and space.

2201.reading: The cool Karunai Ananda muni, the Varuna who came to be seen and worshipped, the rain-cloud of bliss; and dawn-red (2202) his radiance stands.
2201.nuance: கருணை ஆனந்தமுனி gives the guru a fuller name than the ஆனந்தன் of 2171; the Kural's rain that makes virtue possible becomes the guru raining bliss.

2202.reading: Like the great light that stands holding the red radiance of dawn, he is the great one who turns off the glare of maya; and undying (2203) he shows the true thing.
2202.nuance: Maya too has a radiance (பிரகாசம்), and the guru's light is set against it as dawn against lamplight; the attraction of the world is admitted to be bright.

2203.reading: He shows the true substance and takes the servants who long for it as the wealth in his hand, the compassionate one; and he who enjoys (2204) body, wealth and life.
2203.nuance: கைபொருளாய்க் கொண்ட: the disciples are the guru's property, the inverse of 2231 where the disciple is told whom to accept. 2204 then names the three things, body, goods and life, that the disciple gives in return.

2204.reading: He takes body, wealth and life with the water of gift and changes the deeds of the gross body, the leveller; and (2205) he is the vision ida and pingala cannot reach.
2204.nuance: உதகத்தால் கொண்டு, taking with water, is the ritual of giving (the water poured over a gift), so the disciple makes a formal gift of self to the guru, and the guru in return alters the karma. சமனன் may be the impartial one or a form of சமன், Yama, who takes life; the first fits the context.

2205.reading: The vision that ida, pingala and the whirl-point cannot reach, the fierce one who ended lust, murder and theft, and without wavering (2206) he took possession.
2205.nuance: The phrase repeats 2163 almost exactly and applies to the guru what was said of Siva, so that the poem's identification of the two is complete. குடோரி is read as a fierce or formidable one; the word is uncertain. Lust, killing and theft are the three gross sins of the Buddhist and Jain lists too.

2206.reading: I am the servant of the servants who hold to the lotus feet of Chitrambalavan who took me; he took me (2207) though people called me a libertine.
2206.nuance: The first personal statement: the poet places himself under the devotees, not under the guru directly, the adiyaar-of-adiyaar formula of Saiva humility. ஆட்கொண்ட is repeated three times across the unit.

2207.reading: 'This man is a libertine,' people said, and I suffered; everywhere I looked became enemy, I sweated, (2208) was shaken and wept.
2207.nuance: தூர்த்தன் is a wastrel or debauchee; the poet records the charge without denying it. The confession opens an autobiography that 2208 to 2211 continue, unusual in the Siddhar corpus where the self is mostly a cipher.

2208.reading: Shaken, blaming fate, with tears running, confused, I came to the guru's country, and shining before me (2209) I saw the town Kayapuri.
2208.nuance: விதிவிதித்து, cursing or laying it on fate, is the ordinary man's response that the poem leaves behind on reaching the guru's land. குருநாடு may be a region or the guru's domain.

2209.reading: I saw with my eyes the town Kayapuri; I went to that town, was sheltered and settled there; and undying (2210) the Lady named her.
2209.nuance: காயாபுரி may be a real town (a Kayapuri or Kayambur is not securely identified) or the body-city, காயம் being body; the poem's method elsewhere favours the double sense: the poet entered his own body under the guru's teaching. ஆதரித்து, sheltered, is the refuge-taking of a disciple.

2210.reading: The Lady named her Sivananda Valli, the famed Trikonavalli, and with the support of those who study (?) (2211) she raised the daughter of kutilai.
2210.nuance: The Lady, மாது, is the goddess, who names a girl Sivananda Valli; ஓது திரிகோணவல்லி may be the Lady's own name, the goddess of the triangle (which gives the poet his name Thirikonar), or the girl's second name. யூதார் is obscure. The girl is the poem's cipher, raised in 2211 as the daughter of kutilai, the primal power: tradition would take her as the soul, or as kundalini, or as knowledge awakened in the poet.

2211.reading: The daughter of kutilai whom she fondled and raised, she sent to the skilled art of the staff-dance; and gracefully (2212) she danced changing feet.
2211.nuance: குடிலை மகள், daughter of the bent primal power, suggests kundalini or the young goddess (வாலை) of the Siddhars; சிலம்பம் is the staff-dance or martial art, read by tradition as the discipline of breath and body. The plain story, a goddess raising a girl and training her, stands alongside and the poem does not resolve it.

2212.reading: Dancing with changing feet, in the manner of kala and karana, switching above and playing in purity, changing the text (2213) she leapt across many sects.
2212.nuance: கலாதி கரணவிதம்: the dance follows the modes of kala (phase, or the five kalas of the adhvas) and karana (dance-unit, or the inner instruments). சுத்தி விளையாட may be playing in purity or going round (சுற்றி). The dance is read as the soul's play through the tattvas.

2213.reading: Joining in the clasp of hands, she leapt and trod on the body of many sects, treading them under; and gently (2214) she gathered the arts.
2213.nuance: பலசமய மெய்லாகு தாவி அதன் மேல்மிதிக்க: the girl leaps onto the body of the sects and treads on them, which continues 2181's trampling of sect and caste, now as dance. கைலாகு பாய is read as striking a handclasp, a dance gesture.

2214.reading: Gently she gathered the art of bharata dance and the handwork of crores of Vedas, and the words of vows (2215) she spoke herself.
2214.nuance: The girl masters dance and Veda alike; the poem has her acquire every learning before the old woman tells her, in chapter 113, whom among the learned to refuse.

2215.reading: Having studied the southern and northern books, she herself spoke crores of them and the three hundred and thirty (?); and in this land (2216) she made the puppet dance.
2215.nuance: தென்னூல் வடநூல், Tamil and Sanskrit books, are set as equals. முந்நூனூறும் is unclear; a count of texts (three hundred, or the thirty and three hundred) is meant but the figure cannot be fixed.

2216.reading: Made to dance the puppet, the puppet learned also many arts of singing; and known to the land (2217) is Trikonavalli.
2216.nuance: பதுமை, the doll or puppet, is the body moved by the soul in the Siddhar image, or the soul moved by Shakti. Who makes it dance is the Lady; so the girl is the dancer and the puppet is what she animates, which suggests the girl is the inner power and the puppet the body.

2217.reading: I went round the whole grandeur of the north mountain of the renowned Trikonavalli on this earth; and (2218) lightning-like she flashed.
2217.nuance: கிரிகித்தேன் is unclear; I read circumambulating (கிரி, hill, with a verb of going round). The north mountain of the goddess of the triangle may be a shrine hill or, in the body-reading, the head. வம்பி is read as renowned (வம்பு) but may be an epithet of another sense.

2218.reading: Like a cloud that has flashed and spent its lightning, her body cooled, and she knew herself and glowed; and the golden one (2219) looked to her ripeness.
2218.nuance: தன்னை அறிந்த, she knew herself: the end of the girl's training is self-knowledge, and the image of the cloud that has discharged its lightning and grown cool is the calming after awakening. The poem's cipher of the girl here comes closest to the soul.

2219.reading: The old woman who had learned the three gunas, looking at the golden one's ripeness, watched her face till it grew fragrant, cut off the crowd, and (2220) speaks to her.
2219.nuance: முதுகிழவி, the old woman, is the Lady of 2210 seen as the ancient one, Shakti who has mastered the gunas; she tests the girl's readiness (பக்குவம்) before teaching, as a guru does. தொக்கறுத்து is read as cutting off the gathering, that is, taking her aside; the word is uncertain. Her speech runs through chapter 113.

links.note: 2163 said Siva walks at the root beyond the reach of ida, pingala and the whirl-point; 2205 repeats the phrase word for word of the guru, completing the poem's claim that the guru is Siva.
Tirumular says to take a good guru and give him one's goods, body and life; Thirikonar's guru takes body, wealth and life with the water of gift and in exchange alters the disciple's karma.

Arunagirinathar's body slips into the world as a doll of nine gates moved by the rope of breath; Thirikonar's puppet is made to dance by the Lady and learns to sing. Both make the body a puppet, but the Siddhar's puppet learns, where the Thiruppugazh's is only moved.

source_issues: 2199 is a chain of rhyming epithets (பரியான் உரியான் பசியான் பொசியான்) whose sense cannot be fixed; 2210 யூதார், 2215 முந்நூனூறும் and 2217 கிரிகித்தேன் வம்பி are unclear words, probably corrupt.
2218 has a full stop after தளதளத்தாள் in the middle of the second line, the only punctuation in the work; the kalivenba's run-on continues regardless.
